summary: the cases of the krffsmount suite on i686, against kernels whose mount that writes repairs nothing, never sets the dirty flag, and takes a volume without the magic number

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: repairs-nothing
faults.summary: a check that repairs nothing: the mount that writes a dirty volume says that it checked it and leaves its faults in place

faults.name: never-dirty
faults.summary: a dirty flag never set: a mount that writes leaves the volume calling itself clean, so a machine ended while it writes and a write the device fails leave nothing for the next mount to check

faults.name: magic-taken
faults.summary: a magic number never read: a volume whose root lacks it is taken as far as its node chain, which refuses it for another reason
